verdict.label: contradictory
verdict.rationale: Both abstracts report an irisin–triglyceride correlation, but with opposite directions: in Korean overweight/obese children irisin showed a significant inverse correlation with triglycerides (r = -0.331, p = 0.033), whereas in the FPLD2/OND/HC case-control study irisin levels positively correlated with triglyceride levels in the entire study group. The populations (prepubertal children vs. adults with lipodystrophy/obesity/healthy controls) differ, but neither abstract provides a concrete, text-supported contextual difference that explains the opposite directions, so the pair is contradictory.

source_evidence.quote: In the subgroup analyses of overweight/obese children, irisin exhibited a significant inverse correlation with glucose (r = -0.507, p = 0.001) and triglycerides (r = -0.331, p = 0.033).

In the entire study group, irisin levels positively correlated with BMI, lean body mass and index, intra-abdominal/total abdominal fat ratio, triglyceride, cholesterol, insulin, glucose and HbA1c levels.

diagnostics.notes: Extraction verified: side A correctly captures the inverse irisin–triglyceride correlation in overweight/obese children; side B correctly captures the positive irisin–triglyceride correlation in the entire study group. Both are association-type comparisons of the same exposure (irisin) and outcome (triglycerides), so they are comparable. Directions are genuinely opposite. No explicit no-effect conclusion on either side, so not_replicated does not apply. No text-supported explanatory difference is available, so apparent_contradiction is not met.
